l4_steps.name: Initiate structural damage finding report
l4_steps.input: Visual inspection finding, C-check opening discrepancy, or SRM-triggered inspection requirement
l4_steps.output: Damage Finding Report (DFR) with location, area, and initial severity classification
l4_steps.kpi: DFR opened within 2 hours of discovery; 100% of findings logged before repair initiation
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual damage measurement and paper sketches introduce transcription errors when uploaded to AMOS; no integrated photo capture workflow forces separate file attachment steps

l4_steps.name: Define NDT method and inspection scope
l4_steps.input: Damage Finding Report, Aircraft Structural Repair Manual (SRM) Chapter 51, airframe area access card
l4_steps.output: NDT Work Instruction specifying method (UT, ET, RT, PT, MT), zone boundary, and acceptance criteria
l4_steps.kpi: NDT scope defined within 4 hours of DFR; SRM chapter referenced on 100% of instructions
l4_steps.pain_point: Boeing Toolbox revision currency lag — SRM updates from Boeing Service Bulletins (SBs) can trail physical publication by 30–60 days, risking use of superseded acceptance limits

l4_steps.name: Evaluate damage against SRM allowable limits
l4_steps.input: NDT Work Instruction, SRM allowable damage limits, measured damage dimensions
l4_steps.output: Disposition decision: within limits (proceed to NDT), beyond limits (escalate to engineering)
l4_steps.kpi: Disposition decision issued within 8 hours of DFR for non-AOG; 100% of beyond-limit findings escalated same shift
l4_steps.pain_point: Ambiguous SRM allowable tables for compound damage (multiple adjacent findings) require engineering judgement; misclassification risk if junior structures engineers make disposition calls without Level III review

l4_steps.name: Submit damage for engineering disposition review
l4_steps.input: Beyond-limits damage finding, DFR with measurements, photographs, and SRM chapter reference
l4_steps.output: Engineering Disposition Request (EDR) submitted to Structures Engineering queue
l4_steps.kpi: EDR submitted within 2 hours of beyond-limits determination; completeness score ≥95% (all required fields populated)
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS EDR workflow does not integrate directly with OEM damage disposition portals (Boeing SRM Online); engineers must duplicate data entry across two systems, increasing cycle time and error risk

l4_steps.name: Evaluate repair options against approved engineering data
l4_steps.input: Engineering Disposition Request, SRM Chapter 51/53/57, applicable Airworthiness Directives (ADs), fleet history for recurring damage patterns
l4_steps.output: Repair scheme selection: SRM standard repair, SRM alternative repair, or DER-designed repair
l4_steps.kpi: Engineering disposition issued within 24 hours for non-AOG; 100% of dispositions reference specific SRM paragraph or approved data source
l4_steps.pain_point: Recurring structural damage at frame stations may indicate systemic fatigue or corrosion issues not captured in individual DFRs; lack of fleet-level damage trending in Boeing Toolbox means repeat repairs go undetected without manual cross-referencing

l4_steps.name: Determine if OEM or DER engineering order is required
l4_steps.input: Repair scheme assessment, FAA DER authority scope, airline DER/ODA delegation matrix
l4_steps.output: Decision: issue in-house Structural Repair Order (SRO) or submit to Boeing/OEM for Engineering Order (EO)
l4_steps.kpi: OEM referral decision made within 4 hours of disposition review; 0 instances of in-house repair where OEM EO was required by AD or AWL
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines with limited ODA (Organization Designation Authorization) scope must route repairs to Boeing, incurring 5–15 business day lead times that drive AOG extensions; DER authority matrix not always current in AMOS, causing avoidable OEM referrals

l4_steps.name: Issue Structural Repair Order and material requirements
l4_steps.input: Approved repair scheme (SRM, in-house EO, or OEM EO), DFR, parts availability from stores
l4_steps.output: Structural Repair Order (SRO) with step-by-step instructions, material list (alloys, fasteners, sealants), tooling requirements, and inspector hold points
l4_steps.kpi: SRO issued within 2 hours of disposition approval; material list completeness ≥98% (no unplanned AOG parts requests during repair)
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS material reservation does not lock AOG-priority alloy sheet stock, allowing concurrent heavy-check work orders to consume materials needed for structural repairs, causing unplanned procurement delays

l4_steps.name: Assign certified NDT Level II/III inspector to task
l4_steps.input: NDT Work Instruction, inspector qualification matrix (NAS410 / EN4179 certifications), shift roster
l4_steps.output: Inspector assignment confirmed; qualification verified against required NDT method and aircraft type
l4_steps.kpi: Inspector assigned within 1 hour of work instruction release; 100% of assignments verified against NAS410 certification currency
l4_steps.pain_point: NDT Level II/III certifications require 24-month renewal (NAS410); gaps in recency tracking within AMOS qualification module mean expired or method-restricted inspectors may be assigned without automated block, creating FAA Part 145 compliance exposure

l4_steps.name: Execute NDT inspection per approved work instruction
l4_steps.system: Olympus OmniScan (UT/PAUT) integrated with AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware
l4_steps.input: NDT Work Instruction, calibration standards, aircraft access (panels removed, surface prepared), ambient condition log (temperature, humidity)
l4_steps.output: Raw NDT data file, calibration record, inspection coverage map, preliminary indication report
l4_steps.kpi: Coverage rate ≥100% of defined zone (no uninspected area); calibration performed every 4 hours or per shift change; scan data archived within 30 minutes of inspection completion
l4_steps.pain_point: Phased-array UT (PAUT) equipment data files (Olympus OmniScan .evo format) are not natively ingestible by AMOS, requiring manual transcription of indication sizes and locations — primary source of sizing errors reported in ASIAS NDT occurrence database

l4_steps.name: Assess NDT findings against work instruction acceptance criteria
l4_steps.input: NDT indication report, acceptance criteria from SRM or EO, prior repair history at location
l4_steps.output: Accept / reject determination; if additional damage found beyond initial scope, updated DFR issued
l4_steps.kpi: Level III review completed within 4 hours of inspection; 0 indications accepted beyond SRM limits without engineering sign-off
l4_steps.pain_point: Secondary damage found during NDT (e.g., cracking beyond a corrosion blister) resets the engineering disposition cycle, adding 24–72 hours to check schedule with no pre-planned buffer in most C-check work packages

l4_steps.name: Archive NDT findings and close NDT work card
l4_steps.input: Accepted NDT indication report, calibration records, coverage maps, inspector sign-off
l4_steps.output: Closed NDT work card with digital signature; scan data archived to aircraft records in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Work card closed within 2 hours of Level III acceptance; 100% of scan data files attached to aircraft serial number record
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS document storage size limits (per-record attachment caps) require off-system archiving of large PAUT data files to network shares, breaking single-source traceability and complicating FAA audit responses

l4_steps.name: Procure certified repair materials and special fasteners
l4_steps.system: SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO) integrated with AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware
l4_steps.input: Structural Repair Order material list, stores inventory status, certified material certifications (Mill Certs, C of C)
l4_steps.output: Issued materials kitted and delivered to work stand; material traceability records (batch numbers, C of C) linked to SRO in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Material kitting completed within 4 hours of SRO release for planned repairs; 100% of issued materials have traceable Certificate of Conformance
l4_steps.pain_point: High-strength aluminium alloy sheet (2024-T3, 7075-T6) and titanium fasteners have long procurement lead times (8–16 weeks); inadequate buffer stock planning in SAP MRP causes AOG parts requests that extend check TAT by 3–5 days

l4_steps.name: Execute structural repair per approved Structural Repair Order
l4_steps.input: Structural Repair Order, approved engineering data (SRM/EO), issued materials, calibrated tooling (torque wrenches, drill jigs)
l4_steps.output: Completed repair with installed doublers/patches/fasteners per SRO specifications
l4_steps.kpi: Repair step completion sign-off within SRO-defined sequence; 0 out-of-sequence step completions; fastener installation torque within ±10% of SRM specification
l4_steps.pain_point: Complex composite-to-metal bonded repairs require temperature-controlled adhesive curing (120°C bond-line) with limited cure oven capacity during peak C-check input; scheduling conflicts with concurrent composites repairs delay structural repair cycle by 12–24 hours

l4_steps.name: Verify repair dimensions and load path restoration
l4_steps.input: Completed repair assembly, SRO dimensional tolerances, engineering drawing, calibrated measurement tools
l4_steps.output: Dimensional check record; pass/fail determination; rework instruction issued if out of tolerance
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of SRO-defined hold points signed before next step begins; dimensional non-conformance rate <2% of structural repair work orders
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS hold-point enforcement relies on inspector discipline — system allows step sign-off without prior hold-point completion if sequences are not correctly locked, enabling inadvertent bypass of critical structural inspection gates

l4_steps.name: Apply corrosion inhibitor and sealant compound
l4_steps.input: Approved repair with completed dimensional check, SRM-specified sealant (PR-1422, EC-776), surface preparation requirements
l4_steps.output: Sealed repair with corrosion protection applied; sealant cure time logged; area prepared for final NDT verification
l4_steps.kpi: Sealant applied within 30 minutes of surface preparation (ASTM D1002 open-time limit); cure time logged per batch number; 100% coverage of faying surfaces per SRM specification
l4_steps.pain_point: Sealant pot-life management under hangar temperature variations (summer: 35°C+) accelerates cure and reduces workable window; inadequate ambient monitoring in maintenance hangars leads to sealant application beyond open-time limits, requiring removal and rework

l4_steps.name: Perform post-repair NDT verification scan
l4_steps.system: Olympus OmniScan (UT/PAUT) integrated with AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware
l4_steps.input: Completed sealed repair, post-repair NDT Work Instruction, original pre-repair baseline scan data for comparison
l4_steps.output: Post-repair NDT report confirming no sub-surface anomalies, fastener hole integrity, and bondline continuity
l4_steps.kpi: Post-repair scan coverage ≥100% of repair footprint + 25mm margin; indication-free result confirmed on 100% of primary structural repairs before inspector sign-off
l4_steps.pain_point: Sealant application over fastener rows reduces PAUT coupling effectiveness, causing near-surface dead zones that may mask shallow cracking at fastener holes; no airline-standardised post-sealant scan procedure in SRM forces ad-hoc method selection by NDT Level III

l4_steps.name: Quality inspector independent review and dual sign-off
l4_steps.input: Completed SRO work card, NDT pre- and post-repair reports, material traceability records, dimensional check records, engineering EO or SRM reference
l4_steps.output: Quality release stamp on SRO; airworthiness release authorisation issued or corrective action required
l4_steps.kpi: Independent QA review completed within 4 hours of last work card sign-off; QA deficiency rate <1% of released structural repair work orders
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual-sign requirements under FAR Part 145 and EASA Part-145 mandate independent inspection, but AMOS does not prevent the original mechanic from also serving as the independent inspector if role segregation is not enforced at the user account level — a recurring finding in FAA Part 145 audits

l4_steps.name: Verify documentation completeness and regulatory compliance
l4_steps.input: Closed SRO with all work cards, NDT reports, material certs, dimensional records, engineer EO sign-off, QA release stamp
l4_steps.output: Documentation compliance check result; return to service approval issued or documentation deficiency log created for correction
l4_steps.kpi: Documentation review completed within 2 hours of QA release; 0 aircraft released to service with open documentation deficiencies
l4_steps.pain_point: Structural repairs subject to Airworthiness Limitation (AWL) items require recurring inspection intervals to be loaded into AMOS task scheduling at time of repair closure — failure to create the repeat task results in missed mandatory AWL inspections, a critical safety and Part 121 compliance failure

l4_steps.name: Update airworthiness records and issue RTS authorisation
l4_steps.input: Approved documentation package, recurring inspection task creation confirmation (if AWL-driven), aircraft maintenance record
l4_steps.output: Aircraft maintenance record updated; Structural Repair Register entry created; FAA Form 337 (if DER repair) filed; Return to Service (RTS) authorisation signed
l4_steps.kpi: RTS issued within 1 hour of documentation approval; 100% of DER repairs accompanied by filed FAA Form 337 within 8 hours of RTS; AWL recurring tasks created and confirmed in AMOS for 100% of limit-item repairs
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA Form 337 electronic filing via FAA ACAIS portal is not integrated with AMOS, requiring manual data re-entry and introducing 2–4 hour delays at peak check closure periods; lost or misfiled 337s create airworthiness record gaps that require costly FAA coordination to resolve
